He was repeatedly enfeoffed until made Duke of Renguo.
He was repeatedly enfeoffed until made Duke of Ren.
任國公 is Duke of Ren, not Duke of Renguo.
He soon joined the campaign against Liu Heita at Mozhou and, on the army's return, was made Bearer of the Battle-Axe General.
He soon joined the campaign against Liu Heita at Mingzhou and, on the army's return, was made General Who Bears the Axe.
洺州 is Mingzhou, not Mozhou.
Soon he followed in striking Liu Heita at Mozhou; when the army returned, he was appointed Bearer of the Battle-Axe General.
Soon he followed in striking Liu Heita at Mingzhou; when the army returned, he was appointed General Who Bears the Axe.
洺州 is Mingzhou, not Mozhou.

In the ninth year he was made Duke of Kui with hereditary rights to the Langzhou prefecture, though the hereditary appointment was not exercised per precedent.
夔國公 is Duke of Kui. Kuiguo translates 國 a second time.

In the ninth year he was re-enfeoffed as Duke of Kui with hereditary appointment as prefect of Lang Prefecture, but by precedent this hereditary office was not carried out.
夔國公 is Duke of Kui, not Duke of Kuiguo.

Gaozong mourned him with a three-day suspension of court, posthumously made him Commander Unequalled in Honor and Area Commander of Bingzhou, had him buried at Zhaoling with a commemorative stele, and granted the posthumous name Xiang.

Gaozong held mourning for him, suspended court for three days, posthumously granted him Grand Master for the Palace with Golden Bangle and Area Commander of Bing Prefecture, buried him alongside Zhaoling, had a stele erected for him, and gave him the posthumous name Xiang.

Gaozong held mourning for him, suspended court for three days, posthumously granted him Commander Unequalled in Honor and Area Commander of Bingzhou, buried him alongside Zhaoling, had a stele erected for him, and gave him the posthumous name Xiang.
開府儀同三司 is not the Golden Bangle title.
His son Renshi inherited the title and rose to captain in the Left Guard of the Hall of Military Affairs.
His son Renshi inherited the title and rose to Commandant of the Left Dianrong Guard.
左典戎衛郎將 is Commandant of the Left Dianrong Guard, not a captain in a Hall of Military Affairs.
His son Renshi inherited the title and rose to Captain of the Left Guard of the Hall of Military Affairs.
His son Renshi inherited the title and rose to Commandant of the Left Dianrong Guard.
左典戎衛郎將 is not the Hall of Military Affairs.
Yin Qiao, styled Kaishan, came from Hu County in Yong Prefecture and was a grandson of Bu Hai, Chen's Minister of the Court of the Imperial Granaries.

Yin Qiao, styled Kaishan, was a native of Hu County in Yong Prefecture and a grandson of Buhai, Minister of the Court of the Imperial Granaries of Chen.
不害 is Buhai, not Bu Hai.

秘書丞 belongs to the Palace Library, not the Secretariat.
He joined the campaign against Xue Ju as army supervisor on the grand marshal's staff.
He joined the campaign against Xue Ju as adjutant on the grand marshal's staff.
元帥府司馬 is the marshal's adjutant, not an army supervisor.
He followed in striking Xue Ju and served as Army Supervisor of the Grand Marshal's headquarters.
He followed in striking Xue Ju and served as Adjutant of the Grand Marshal's headquarters.
司馬 is adjutant, not Army Supervisor.

They duly drew up at Zhezhi, Ju seized the opportunity, and the army suffered a crushing defeat.
折墌 is Zhezhi, the same 墌 as Gaozhi, not Zhedi.

Thereupon they arrayed troops at Zhezhi, were exploited by Ju, and the army was utterly defeated.

Taizong came in person to mourn him and wept bitterly, posthumously making him Right Vice Director of the Branch Department east of the Shan Pass and granting the posthumous name Jie.

Taizong personally attended the mourning, wept with great grief, posthumously granted him Right Vice Commissioner of the Shandong Grand Commissioner, and gave the posthumous name Jie.
Taizong personally attended the mourning, wept with great grief, posthumously granted him Right Vice Director of the Branch Department east of the Shan Pass, and gave him the posthumous name Jie.
僕射 is Vice Director, and 陝東 is not Shandong.

In Zhenguan 14 an edict ordered that he, alongside the posthumously honored Sikong Prince Huai'an Li Shentong, Sikong Prince of Hejian Li Xiaogong, and Minister of the Board of Revenue Liu Zhenghui, all share sacrifices in Gaozu's temple for their founding service.

In the fourteenth year of Zhenguan an edict ordered that he, together with the posthumously granted Minister of Works Prince Huai'an Li Shentong, the posthumously granted Minister of Works Prince of Hejian Li Xiaogong, and the posthumously granted Minister of Revenue Liu Zhenghui, all for founding merit share sacrifices in Gaozu's temple hall.
司空 is Minister of Works, not an untranslated Sikong.

In the seventeenth year he was also, together with Zhangsun Wuji, Tang Jian, Zhangsun Shunde, Liu Hongji, Liu Zhenghui, Chai Shao, and others, seventeen in all, portrayed in likeness at the Lingyan Pavilion.
十七人 is the total, not six named men plus fourteen others.

In Yonghui 5 he was posthumously honored as Minister of Works.
司空 is Minister of Works.

In the fifth year of Yonghui he was posthumously granted Minister of Works.
司空 is Minister of Works, not an untranslated Sikong.

Qiao's younger clansman Wenli was a man of letters who served as Companion of the Heir Apparent in the Wude era, began compiling the History of Liang, and died before finishing it.
太子中舍人 is Companion of the Heir Apparent, not a vague crown-prince attendant.

Qiao's younger cousin of the same clan Wenli had literary talent; in the Wude era he served as Companion of the Heir Apparent, compiled the History of Liang, and died before completing it.
太子中舍人 is Companion of the Heir Apparent.

Under the Sui in the Daye era, Zhenghui served as adjutant of the Taiyuan Soaring Hawk Garrison.

Zhenghui, in the Daye era of Sui, served as Adjutant of the Soaring Hawk Garrison of Taiyuan.
鷹揚 is Soaring Hawk, not Hawk-raising.

Someone reported this; Taizong, knowing the urgency, wished to strike first and kill them, and so dispatched Zhenghui with an urgent memorial to the garrison headquarters reporting that Wei and the other two men plotted rebellion.

Someone reported this; Taizong, knowing the urgency, wished to strike first and kill them, and so dispatched Zhenghui with an urgent memorial to the garrison headquarters reporting that Wei and one other, two men in all, plotted rebellion.
威等二人 is two men, Wei and one other, not Wei plus two others.
When the Generalissimo's headquarters was established, he was appointed registrar of the Household Bureau.
When the Generalissimo's headquarters was established, he was appointed administrator of the Revenue Section.
戶曹參軍 is the revenue section of the headquarters, not a Household Bureau. 曹參 here is not the Han minister Cao Can.
When the Generalissimo's headquarters was established he was brought in as Registrar of the Household Bureau.
When the Generalissimo's headquarters was established he was brought in as Administrator of the Revenue Section.
戶曹 is the revenue section, not the Household Bureau.
He served successively as Minister of Justice and Minister of the Court of Imperial Banquets and was enfeoffed as Duke of Xing State.
He served successively as Minister of Justice and Minister of the Court of Imperial Banquets and was enfeoffed as Duke of Xing.
邢國公 is Duke of Xing. Xing State translates 國 a second time.
His son Xuanyi inherited the title, was made Duke of Yu, married Princess Nanping, and was appointed commandant of the emperor's sons-in-law.
His son Xuanyi inherited the title, was made Duke of Yu, married Princess Nanping, and was appointed commandant-escort.
渝國公 is Duke of Yu. 駙馬都尉 is commandant-escort, not a household of the emperor's sons-in-law.
His son Xuanyi inherited the title, was re-enfeoffed as Duke of Yu State, married Princess Nanping, and was appointed Commandant of the Emperor's Son-in-Law's Household.
His son Xuanyi inherited the title, was re-enfeoffed as Duke of Yu, married Princess Nanping, and was appointed commandant-escort.
渝國公 is Duke of Yu, not Duke of Yu State. 駙馬都尉 is commandant-escort.
The second son Qi served as Vice Director of the Bureau of Celestial Offices in the Changshou era and was destroyed by the harsh officials.
The second son Qi served as Vice Minister of Personnel, then called the Celestial Office, in the Changshou era and was destroyed by the harsh officials.
天官 was Wu Zetian's name for the Ministry of Personnel, not a separate Bureau of Celestial Offices.
The second son Qi, in the Changshou era served as Vice Director of the Bureau of Celestial Offices and was trapped by harsh officials.
The second son Qi, in the Changshou era served as Vice Minister of Personnel, then called the Celestial Office, and was trapped by harsh officials.
天官侍郎 is the renamed Vice Minister of Personnel.
His grandfather Lie was a Zhou general of fast cavalry who served as prefect of Sui and Liang prefectures and was enfeoffed as Duke of Guanjun County.
His grandfather Lie was a Zhou general of fast cavalry who served as prefect of Suizhou and Liangzhou and was enfeoffed as Duke of Guanjun County.
遂州 is Suizhou. Rendering it Sui confuses it with the Sui dynasty.
His grandfather Lie was General of Fast Cavalry under Zhou, served successively as prefect of Sui and Liang prefectures, and was enfeoffed as Duke of Guanjun County.
His grandfather Lie was General of Fast Cavalry under Zhou, served successively as prefect of Suizhou and Liangzhou, and was enfeoffed as Duke of Guanjun County.
遂州 is Suizhou, not Sui.
In his youth he served as a guard attendant to the Sui Yuande Crown Prince.
In his youth he served as a swordsman guard to the Sui Yuande Crown Prince.
千牛備身 is the swordsman guard, not a generic guard attendant. 千牛 is not a count of oxen.
In youth he was appointed as Thousand-Ox Guard Attendant to the Yuande Crown Prince of Sui.
In youth he was appointed swordsman guard to the Yuande Crown Prince of Sui.
千牛備身 is the swordsman guard. Thousand-Ox is a false etymology in the translation.
He was appointed chief clerk of the Right Army Aide Staff of the Grand Army Commander.
He was appointed chief administrator of the office of the grand commander of the Right Lingjun Army.
右領軍大都督府長史 is chief administrator of that headquarters, not chief clerk of an Aide Staff.
He was appointed Chief Clerk of the Right Army Aide Staff of the Grand Army Commander.
He was appointed Chief Administrator of the office of the grand commander of the Right Lingjun Army.
長史 is chief administrator, not Chief Clerk of an Aide Staff.

When the Sui general Sang Xianhe attacked, Sun Hua led elite troops across the river to reinforce him. Shao swung his army straight at their rear and, joining Shi Dana, crushed them. Xianhe was routed, and Shao then advanced with the other generals to take the capital.

When the Sui general Sang Xianhe attacked, Sun Hua led elite troops across the river to reinforce the Tang. Shao swung his army straight at the enemy rear and, joining Shi Danai, crushed them. Xianhe was routed, and Shao then advanced with the other generals to take the capital.
孫華 crossed to help the Tang side against Sang Xianhe, not to reinforce Sang. 史大奈 is Shi Danai.

The Sui general Sang Xianhe came to attack; Sun Hua led elite troops across the river to reinforce him. Shao led his army straight to strike their rear, and joining forces with Shi Dana struck them; Xianhe was routed, and he then advanced with the other generals to take the capital.

The Sui general Sang Xianhe came to attack; Sun Hua led elite troops across the river to reinforce the Tang. Shao led his army straight to strike the enemy rear, and joining forces with Shi Danai struck them; Xianhe was routed, and he then advanced with the other generals to take the capital.
援之 is aid to the Tang side. 史大奈 is Shi Danai, not Dana.
In Wude 1 he rose to General-in-Chief of the Left Wing Guard.
In Wude 1 he rose to General-in-chief of the Left Assisting Guard.
左翊衛 is the Left Assisting Guard, not the Left Wing Guard.

In the first year of Wude he was promoted in succession to General-in-chief of the Left Assisting Guard.
翊衛 is the Assisting Guard, not a Wing Guard.

He soon followed Taizong in pacifying Xue Ju, defeating Song Jingang, reducing Wang Shichong at Luoyang, and capturing Dou Jiande at Wulao. He was enfeoffed Duke of Huo with a substantive fief of twelve hundred households and made General-in-chief of the Right Courageous Guard.

Soon he followed Taizong in pacifying Xue Ju, defeating Song Jingang, attacking and pacifying Wang Shichong at Luoyang, and capturing Dou Jiande at Wulao; he was enfeoffed Duke of Huo, granted a substantive fief of twelve hundred households, and transferred to General-in-chief of the Right Courageous Guard.

In the seventh year he was advanced to Grand General of Garrison Troops, acted as General-in-Chief of the Right Xiaowei Guard, and was re-enfeoffed Duke of Qiao.
In the seventh year he was advanced to General of Garrisoned Troops, acted as General-in-chief of the Right Courageous Guard, and was re-enfeoffed Duke of Qiao.
右驍衛 is the Right Courageous Guard, not Xiaowei.
In the seventh year he was advanced to Grand General of Garrison Troops, acted as General-in-Chief of the Right Xiaowei Guard, and his enfeoffment was changed to Duke of Qiao.
In the seventh year he was advanced to General of Garrisoned Troops, acted as General-in-chief of the Right Courageous Guard, and his enfeoffment was changed to Duke of Qiao.

Wu Shihuo was a native of Wenshui in Bing Prefecture.

When Gaozu first marched through Fen and Jin, he lodged at Shiyi's home;
When Gaozu first marched through Fen and Jin, he lodged at Shihuo's home;

When Gaozu first marched through Fen and Jin, he rested at Shiyi's home;
When Gaozu first marched through Fen and Jin, he rested at Shihuo's home;
士鸊 is 彠, Wu Shihuo. The English Shiyi belongs to his brother 士逸.
where Gaozu favored him. When Gaozu became Taiyuan garrison commander, Shiyi was brought in as army equipment officer on the campaign staff.
where Gaozu favored him. When Gaozu became Taiyuan garrison commander, Shihuo was brought in as army equipment officer on the campaign staff.

there he received Gaozu's attention and favor, and when Gaozu became Taiyuan garrison commander, Shiyi was brought in as Army Equipment Officer in the campaign staff.
there he received Gaozu's attention and favor, and when Gaozu became Taiyuan garrison commander, Shihuo was brought in as Army Equipment Officer in the campaign staff.

At that time bandits swarmed everywhere; Shiyi once secretly urged Gaozu to raise troops and himself presented military texts and portents. Gaozu said to him: "Please say no more.
At that time bandits swarmed everywhere; Shihuo once secretly urged Gaozu to raise troops and himself presented military texts and portents. Gaozu said to him: "Please say no more.

Wang Wei and Gao Junya secretly told Shihuo, "Hongji and the others all evaded the third campaign levy. Their offense warrants death—how can they be allowed to lead troops?

Wang Wei and Gao Junya secretly said to Shiyi: "Hongji and the others all evaded the third campaign levy—they have committed offenses warranting death; how can they lead troops?
Wang Wei and Gao Junya secretly said to Shihuo: "Hongji and the others all evaded the third campaign levy—they have committed offenses warranting death; how can they lead troops?

The garrison army affairs officer Tian Deping again wanted to urge Wei and the others to interrogate the recruits. Shihuo told Deping, "The pursuit troops all answer to the Duke of Tang.

When the righteous banner rose, Shiyi was made head of the equipment section in the Grand General's Office.
When the righteous banner rose, Shihuo was made head of the equipment section in the Grand General's Office.

When the righteous banner rose, Shiyi was made Equipment Section head of the Grand General's Office.

At first, when the uprising was about to begin, Shihuo had not been forewarned. After the capital was pacified he claimed, "I once dreamed that Gaozu entered the Western Capital and ascended as Son of Heaven."

Wu Shihuo was among the first to join the uprising and was enfeoffed as a founding meritocrat, yet he did no real work in the struggle and plainly rode others' efforts; other biographies show the praise lavished on him to be excessive.

太子監門率 is Commandant of the Heir Apparent's Gate Guard, not Crown Prince Gate Supervisor.
